_about: Public-domain Richard Allestree (1619-1681), Regius Professor of Divinity at Oxford and Provost of Eton, for the Word Hoard: the devotional books published anonymously as 'by the author of The Whole Duty of Man', and long attributed to him: The Practice of Christian Graces, or The Whole Duty of Man (first edition, 1658), Private Devotions for Several Occasions (1660), The Gentleman's Calling (1660), The Causes of the Decay of Christian Piety (1667) and The Government of the Tongue (fifth impression, after 1674). The attribution is the scholarly consensus, not a title-page statement. Texts are from Internet Archive scans. Added 2026-10-23 by lane A, round 68 (my pick); Adam may veto the whole shelf. Every printing dated before 1930, so public domain in the US. No uids minted.

allestree-practice-christian-graces-1658: The Practice of Christian Graces, or The Whole Duty of Man, with Private Devotions (London: D. Maxwell for T. Garthwait, 1658): the first edition of The Whole Duty of Man
allestree-decay-piety-1667: The Causes of the Decay of Christian Piety (London: R. Norton for T. Garthwait, 1667)
allestree-government-tongue-fifth-impres: The Government of the Tongue, fifth impression (Oxford: at the Theater; title-page date read as M.DC.LXVII, but the imprimatur is dated 24 January 1675 and the book first appeared in 1674, so this printing is 1675 or later)
